title: The Bias-Variance Tradeoff
description: A guide to understanding the tension between bias and variance, and how to find the optimal model complexity.
content:
**The bias-variance tradeoff** is a foundational concept in machine learning that encapsulates the tension between two primary sources of error when building predictive models: bias and variance.

The overall prediction error of a model can be seen as a combination of three components:
• Squared bias
• Variance
• Irreducible error (noise)

**Bias** refers to the error introduced by overly simplistic assumptions in the model.

Key characteristics of high bias:
• Leads to underfitting
• Poor performance on both training and validation data

**Variance** refers to the model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training data.

Key characteristics of high variance:
• Leads to overfitting
• Good performance on training data, but poor performance on validation data

In essence, the bias-variance tradeoff implies that as we reduce bias error, we typically increase the variance error, and vice versa.

Finding the optimal tradeoff involves selecting a model complexity that minimizes the combined error from bias and variance.

Common strategies to manage the bias-variance tradeoff:
• Regularization techniques
• Cross-validation
• Ensemble methods
